title: using and IDisposable (deterministic cleanup)
hook: IDisposable is a contract that says "call Dispose when you are done." The using statement is try/finally that calls Dispose even when the try throws — essential for SkiaSharp surfaces and file streams.

blocks.text: **IDisposable** defines a **Dispose** method for releasing resources deterministically — file handles, network connections, native graphics objects. The **using** statement (or **using declaration**) wraps creation and calls **Dispose** in a finally block, even when an exception escapes. **IAsyncDisposable** and **await using** are the async counterparts for types that need await to close cleanly. Variables declared in a using are read-only; you cannot reassign them.

entries.plainDefinition: A contract with a Dispose method. Call it when you finish with an object that holds unmanaged or scarce resources.
Syntax sugar for try/finally that calls Dispose. The compiler generates the cleanup code.
Async cleanup contract with DisposeAsync. Used with await using.
entries.example: await using var session = await OpenSessionAsync();

entries.plainDefinition: using var x = ...; disposes at the end of the enclosing scope — usually the method.

blocks.text: The garbage collector (GC) eventually collects managed objects, but native memory inside SkiaSharp, database drivers, and socket wrappers is invisible to GC pressure. Without Dispose, a high-concurrency image pipeline leaks native memory while managed heap looks fine. using guarantees cleanup on success, failure, and early return. Finalizers are a last resort — covered in module 14, not here.

blocks.title: Dispose should not throw in ordinary cleanup
blocks.body: Dispose must be safe to call twice (idempotent). Throwing from Dispose during unwind can mask the original exception. Release resources quietly when possible.

items.title: Resource is created
items.body: using var surface = SKSurface.Create(...); assigns the disposable object.

items.title: try body runs
items.body: Your drawing or I/O code executes. If throw occurs, control jumps to finally.

items.title: finally calls Dispose
items.body: The compiler-generated finally invokes Dispose (or DisposeAsync for await using).

items.title: Exception continues if one was thrown
items.body: Dispose runs first; then the original exception propagates up the stack.

diagram.title: using statement expansion
diagram.source:
flowchart TD
  A[using var resource = Create] --> B[try: use resource]
  B -->|success| C[finally: resource.Dispose]
  B -->|throw| D[finally: resource.Dispose]
  D --> E[exception continues up]
  C --> F[continue method]

snippet.explanation: Lines 3–4: every SkiaSharp handle is using-owned. Line 9: return happens after Dispose on inner objects but before surface disposal at scope end. Native memory releases on throw or return.

snippet.label: await using for async cleanup
snippet.explanation: Line 3: await using calls DisposeAsync in finally. Line 6: async cleanup completes before the method continues — important for queue sessions and async streams.

blocks.title: Resource cleanup in C# vs JS/TS
rows: IDisposable + using — decades of daily use
using pattern is well-known; analyzers warn on undisposed IDisposable
No IDisposable in the type system — rely on finally manually
SkiaSharp requires Dispose — GC does not free native memory promptly
Native addons vary; no uniform CLR contract

blocks.title: Creating SKSurface without using
blocks.body: Relying on GC for SkiaSharp leaks native memory under load. Always wrap SKSurface, SKBitmap, SKPaint, and SKCanvas in using.

blocks.title: Returning a disposed object
blocks.body: Do not return an object from inside a using block if the block disposes it before the caller uses it. Dispose at the owner's scope — the type that holds the resource across methods should be IDisposable.

interviewTakeaways: using is try/finally + Dispose; await using is DisposeAsync.
SkiaSharp and other native wrappers require deterministic Dispose.
Finalizers are almost never the answer — module 14.
commonPitfalls: Creating SKSurface without using and relying on GC.
Returning a disposed object from a using block that disposed too early — dispose at the owner's scope.

jsTsCorrelations.note: JavaScript is adding explicit resource management (using, Symbol.asyncDispose). C# has had using/IDisposable for decades and the CLR still has a separate finalizer queue.

jsTsCorrelations.concept: no IDisposable in the type system
jsTsCorrelations.note: TypeScript cannot enforce Dispose. You rely on finally or the new JS using. C# compiler and analyzers support the using pattern for IDisposable.
JavaScript explicit resource management is late and optional. C# using is the daily native-resource pattern for libraries like SkiaSharp.
